subject: Q4 renewal: usage trend & recommended GPU top-up for SkyCloud AI
messages:

To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 renewal discussion

Thanks for the heads up, Marissa — appreciate the usage breakdown you sent earlier. Quick context from our side: we shipped a latency-sensitive recommendation engine in early Aug and have seen a sustained 42% increase in concurrent generation requests during peak hours (17:00-21:00 UTC). Our on-call noticed a handful of OOM-triggered fallbacks to a lower-capacity model last week (logs attached to internal ticket).

Short version: we want to avoid more fallbacks as traffic increases. We have a renewal window at the end of Sept and are open to expanding committed capacity. Can you outline what an aggressive top-up would look like (target SLA 99.5% p95 < 250ms) and the procurement steps? Happy to schedule a 30-min sync next week.

— Sana
Principal ML Engineer
SkyCloud AI

Cc: SkyCloud Ops <ops@skycloud.ai>

Thanks, Sana — that matches what our telemetry shows. Attaching a short usage summary (hourly spike distribution + kernel saturation charts) and a single-page proposal for an expedited top-up. High-level proposal: +16 GPUs (A100-equivalent) as a short-term tranche for the next 3 months, with an option to convert to a committed Dedicated slab at renewal. That config hits your 99.5% p95 target in our staging load tests.

Procurement steps we recommend:
- Sign a one-page addendum to lock the tranche for 3 months.
- Provide a PO referencing RDW-5231.
- We'll schedule a rollback window and observability dashboard share.

I'll loop in our renewal lead and solutions engineer to confirm sizing and pricing. Can you send the PO cadence (Net 30 / Net 45) and any internal procurement constraints?

Best,
Marissa Cole

Team — forwarding SkyCloud's note and our staging results. Key telemetry: 42% peak increase, p95 latency slipping toward 320–380ms under current provision during spike windows, KV cache hit rate 78% (we can tune), and GPU SM utilization intermittently at 86–94% on the heaviest workloads.

Ask:
- Ben: confirm whether +16 A100-eq over 3 months is the right tranche vs. +12 with aggressive autoscale policies. Include a quick cost delta for (short-term tranche) vs (committed 12-mo slab).
- Karthik: if they want to convert to a committed slab at renewal, what cadence/discount bands should we propose (they're mid-market with enterprise procurement)?
- Neha: operational checklist — observability playbook, rollback SLA, and runbook handoff.

I proposed the addendum + PO flow to Sana, but let's not surface pricing until we align.

— Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-17T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Q4 renewal discussion — sizing input needed

Marissa / team — I ran a quick capacity model using their telemetry and our kernel saturation profiles. Notes:
- With current workload burst profile, +12 A100-eq (with aggressive continuous batching and prefix KV tuning) would reduce p95 to ~210–230ms in prod but leaves <5% risk of transient fallbacks during 1-2 hour sustained spikes.
- +16 GPUs gives more headroom for a conservative rollout and keeps p95 comfortably under 200ms in our simulated peak. It also reduces sustained core utilization to ~68–72%, which helps kernel warm-up and reduces tail variance.
- Cost delta (3-month tranche): +12 GPUs = $XX,XXX/mo; +16 GPUs = +$YY,YYY/mo. (I'll attach a formal price sheet once we lock tranche length.)

Recommendation: Offer them two options in the addendum: (A) +12 GPUs with a conversion clause to commit to 12-mo slab at renewal with a conversion credit; (B) +16 GPUs as a temporary immediate buffer, convertible to a larger slab with a smaller credit. Option A is more price-efficient now; Option B is lower risk for their latency SLO.

Cc: Neha — operational readiness checks below look fine; will need a 2-hour maintenance window to bring the tranche online and a 24h observational hold for SLA measurement.

— Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Patel <sana@skycloud.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, SkyCloud Ops <ops@skycloud.ai>
Date: 2027-09-22T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 renewal discussion

Sana — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on your PO cadence (Net 30) and the risk tolerance you described on the call, attached is a concise addendum with both tranche options and the conversion language Ben proposed. TL;DR:
- Option A (cost-savvy): +12 A100-eq GPUs for 3 months; conversion credit toward a 12-mo committed slab at renewal. Estimated incremental run rate: $XX,XXX/mo.
- Option B (latency-first): +16 A100-eq GPUs for 3 months; minimal risk of fallbacks and p95 target comfortably met. Estimated incremental run rate: $YY,YYY/mo.

Next steps:
1) You confirm which option you prefer; we finalize the addendum and get it countersigned.
2) Provide PO referenced to RDW-5231 (Net 30).
3) We schedule a 2-hour window for tranche activation and handover to SkyCloud Ops; we'll monitor for 48h and share a p95 report.

Attached: SkyCloud_Renewal_Proposal_Q4-2027.pdf (includes the addendum drafts and a one-page utilization appendix). Let me know if you want us to price a 6-month tranche instead — that reduces monthly delta by ~12% vs 3 months.

Best,
